root_cause.text: nft_dynset_expr_setup() in nf_tables failed to unwind partially cloned stateful expressions in a set element when a later nft_expr_clone(GFP_ATOMIC) call failed, leaving previously cloned expressions in nft_set_elem_expr leaked on the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “If cloning the second stateful expression … fails, then the first stateful expression remains in place without being released,” and the patch changes nft_dynset_expr_setup() from immediately returning on clone failure to jumping to err_out and calling nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(&ctx, elem_expr).

intent_record.intent_summary: Export a dedicated nft set element expression destroy helper to allow proper cleanup of element expressions.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, `void nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(const struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set_elem_expr *elem_expr);`, was added to the header alongside the existing set element expression helper declarations.
intent_record.how: This exposes a dedicated destroy helper for `nft_set_elem_expr` objects so other compilation units can call it, enabling proper cleanup of set element expressions at runtime where previously only clone and broader element destroy interfaces were declared.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export nft_set_elem_expr_destroy by removing its file-local static qualifier so it can be called from other source files.
intent_record.what: The function definition of nft_set_elem_expr_destroy was changed by removing the static storage-class specifier, making it externally visible, while keeping its name, parameters, and body unchanged apart from indentation adjustment.
intent_record.how: This allows nft_set_elem_expr_destroy to be referenced from other translation units instead of being limited to the current source file, enabling external callers to invoke the same destruction logic without changing its runtime behavior internally.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clean up partially cloned dynset element expressions on clone failure by destroying the accumulated expression state before returning an error.
intent_record.what: The function `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` now creates a local `struct nft_ctx ctx` initialized from `priv->set->net` and `priv->set->table->family`, changes the `nft_expr_clone()` failure path from `return -1;` to `goto err_out;`, and adds an `err_out` label that calls `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(&ctx, elem_expr)` before returning `-1`.
intent_record.how: If cloning one of the element expressions fails after earlier clones have already succeeded, the function now cleans up the partially built `elem_expr` state before returning an error, preventing leaked or stale cloned expressions from remaining allocated.

grouping_result.intent: Clean up partially cloned dynset element expressions on clone failure by destroying the accumulated expression state before returning an error.

Author: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

    netfilter: nftables: generalize set extension to support for several expressions
    
    This patch replaces NFT_SET_EXPR by NFT_SET_EXT_EXPRESSIONS. This new
    extension allows to attach several expressions to one set element (not
    only one single expression as NFT_SET_EXPR provides). This patch

bic_trace_step.reason: The added helper `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` contains the relevant error-path logic in full, so the snippet is sufficient. In that function, it loops over multiple expressions: `for (i = 0; i < priv->num_exprs; i++) { ... if (nft_expr_clone(expr, priv->expr_array[i]) < 0) return -1; elem_expr->size += priv->expr_array[i]->ops->size; }`. This shows the vulnerable construct: when cloning one expression fails, the function immediately `return -1` without unwinding or destroying any expressions that were successfully cloned in earlier iterations. Because `elem_expr->size` is incremented after each successful clone, previously cloned stateful expressions can already be present in the set element when a later clone fails, matching the stated root cause. The caller `nft_dynset_new()` does `if (priv->num_exprs && nft_dynset_expr_setup(priv, ext) < 0) goto err2;`, but no cleanup of partially cloned expressions is shown before the error path. There is no rollback loop or destroy helper in `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` for already cloned entries, so the fix is not present.
